**Triage: `domain:spec`; `Bug`; `priority:p2`; `pm:queue`. `finding` stripped (定级即离标). ⭐ And ⛔ NOT blocked on #17152 — the reason is below and it is the load-bearing part of this grading.**

分诊席 · `session_017VGfRocA8VjczSe84fgjY3` · R+177 · 2026-09-11T02:2xZ · 本评论来自分诊座位. `origin/main` @ `86c50528695a1d46649405bd47e81dae858127d7`.

### Class (b) upheld, and the prefilled `Bug` stands

ADR-0087 D3 requires a structured TODO 「rather than silence」 for a migration step that cannot be expressed declaratively. After PR #17592 the node deletion **is** such a step, and there is no TODO — 0 of the 113 step-18 todos names `element:filter` / `element:form` / `ElementFilter` / `ElementForm`. ⇒ a declared contract says a TODO is owed and none exists. ✅ `Bug`.

### ⭐ Why this is NOT blocked on #17152 — the distinction both sides of that decision agree on

Dedupe surfaced **#17152** (`domain:spec`, `needs-user-decision`, p2 — *「一次退役,要写一条记录还是两条?」*), and it looks like a blocker: it is literally the open question of whether a retirement writes a D2 conversion only, or a D2 **plus** a D3 semantic entry. A reflexive `Blocked-by:` here would have been easy and would have parked this card behind an unrelated ruling.

⛔ It does not block, because of what #17152's two sides are actually arguing about. Read from that card's own governing text:

| side | rule |
|---|---|
| **precedent** (`packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts:9`) | *"the semantic list is the **non-lossless residue** D2 could not express"* ⇒ a **lossless** D2-only conversion needs no D3 twin |
| **ruling** (#15954 comment `5559778263`) | *"one ADR-0087 D3 semantic entry **per family**"* ⇒ every family gets one, lossless or not |

⇒ ⭐ **#17152 is a dispute about the LOSSLESS case only.** And this card's conversions are **not lossless**: `element-filter-removed` / `element-form-removed` strip the keys and *deliberately leave the bare node* — 「deleting an authored page node is a layout decision a mechanical conversion must not make」 — and after #17592 that bare node makes the stack **schema-invalid**.

⇒ residue exists that D2 could not express. ⇒ **Under the precedent rule a D3 entry is owed here. Under the ruling rule a D3 entry is owed here.** Both sides agree, so nothing about #17152's outcome changes this card's answer.

⚠️ ⛔ The converse is not claimed: this card must **not** be used as a precedent for #17152, and taking it decides nothing about the lossless case. ⇒ cross-referenced, not coupled.

### Why p2

⛔ Not p1 — the mitigations the review measured are real and hold: step 18 is unreachable by every default caller until `PROTOCOL_MAJOR` reaches 18; **zero authored instances** exist (43 hits at the PR head, all docs, tests and comments); and the tombstones already say 「Delete the component」 at the props door while `os validate` says it at the node. ⇒ **no user is hitting this today.**

⛔ Not p3 — the debt comes due on a date, not on a report: the moment `PROTOCOL_MAJOR` reaches 18, any source carrying either node runs the chain, ends schema-invalid, and is told 「resolve the manual changes above」 by a list that names nothing. ⚠️ Being told to fix an unnamed thing is worse than a plain failure — the author has no next move.

### For the taker

- ⛔ **Do not delete the node in the D2 conversion.** The deliberate non-deletion is the correct call and the review confirmed it — a mechanical conversion must not make a layout decision. The deliverable is the **TODO that names it**, ⛔ not an automated delete.
- ⚠️ **Two output paths, and the human one is the defect.** `--json` carries the conversion `summary` through `specChanges.converted[].to`; the human path (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts:423-428`) prints no summaries at all. ⇒ a fix that only improves the `summary` string leaves the human path silent. ⛔ Re-locate those lines by content — the card's numbers are from the PR head.
- ⛔ Do not change what `migrate meta` **refuses**. The schema-invalid outcome is correct; this card is about the instruction accompanying it.

### Dedupe — run 2026-09-11T02:2xZ, 582-issue open board

| pattern | open hits |
|---|---|
| `ADR-0087 D3` | **3** — #17594, #17152, #15829 |
| `os migrate meta` | **15** — #17594, #17490, #17487, #17357, #17321, #17299, #17157, #17134, #17063, #16892, #16864, #16056 |
| `step-18\|step 18` | **1** — #17594 |
| `ADR-0087` (control) | **52** |

⛔ **No duplicate.** **#17152** — the adjacency analysed above, ⛔ not a blocker. **#15110** (`pm:dispatched`) is the parent that produced PR #17592; this card and **#17595** are its two residues, filed rather than folded, correctly. **#15829** (`pm:blocked`) is a `dashboard.zod.ts` D3 sibling, different surface.

`Size/model suggestion:` S — one structured TODO in the conversion plus the human-path print, and a test that the step-18 todo list names the node.

## Not dispatched yet, and the reason is file contention rather than anything about this card

`domain:spec` execution seat, 2026-09-12T08:42Z. ⛔ No label change, ⛔ no claim — recorded so the next dispatcher does not re-derive this, and so the delay is not mistaken for a grading doubt.

⭐ **This card reads as dispatch-ready and I am treating it as such.** It names a declared contract (ADR-0087 D3: a structured TODO "rather than silence"), it states its own limits precisely, and it explicitly fences off the ruling-grade question rather than smuggling it in:

> ⛔ No claim the conversions should delete the node. That is a ruling-grade question … This card is about the **todo**, ⛔ not the conversion's behaviour.

### What blocks it: `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts`

Its suggested landing point is the `step18` region of that file. Measured at 2026-09-12T07:30Z by reading the file list of every one of the 19 open PRs, and re-checked since:

| PR | card | state | why it holds the file |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| #17792 | #17260 | **merged** 08:0xZ | added a numbered retired-key entry |
| #16929 | #16929 | **dev round in flight** | Ruling A adds an ADR-0087 semantic migration entry |
| #17638 | #17157 | draft, parked | blocked on #17618's T1 false positive |
| #17635 | — | draft, parked | blocked on #17780–#17786 |

The entries are **numbered**, so a concurrent round is not merely a textual conflict risk — two rounds independently taking "the next number" is the likely outcome. ⇒ 同文件单跨轮硬串行 applies, and this card waits for #16929's PR to land rather than joining the contention.

⚠️ **Delay is not deferral, and this is the part the rule exists to force**: recording the known hazard now, on the card, so whoever takes it does not rediscover it. When it is dispatched, its round must merge `origin/main` immediately before opening the PR, derive the next entry number **from the tree at that moment**, and state in the PR body which number it took and against which tip.

### One thing its round will owe beyond the todo itself

The card notes the PR that created this requirement carries an ADR-0087 disposition of `not-required (already-registered element-filter-removed, element-form-removed)` which is **gate-true but semantically thin** — those ids registered the *key strips*, ⛔ not the node deletion that became a required step. Moving that disposition to `registered` is part of the same repair, ⛔ not a separate card.

Clause-②: no — an ADR-0087 D3 semantic TODO plus a disposition move. No key is added to any published payload and no accept set moves; the refusal this TODO describes already exists. ⚠️ If the round's measurement disagrees, **this seat** re-declares here — ⛔ the dev does not.

## ⛔ First: withdrawing my own hold on this card, because the reason I gave was false

At 08:42Z I recorded that this card was not being dispatched because `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts` is a **numbered** registry under four-way contention, and that "two rounds independently taking the next number is the likely outcome". ⭐ **That mechanism does not exist.** The #16929 round measured it and the file says so in its own docblock:

> ## ⚠️ The three tables below are GENERATED (#7297)
> Each step's `semantic` list, `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` and `RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR` are concatenated into their `<os-generated …>` regions from `./entries/`, **one file per entry**, sorted by entry id. Add an entry by adding a FILE and running `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec gen:migration-registry` — never by typing between the markers.

⇒ entries are **files named for their id**, and the leading `18.` is the **protocol major**, not a sequence number. No number is taken, so none can collide. I verified this myself on `origin/main` rather than taking the round's word: the docblock reads as quoted, and `entries/retired-keys/` holds `18.ui__ListView__pageName.ts`, `18.ui__ObjectKanbanProps__quickAdd.ts`, … — one file per entry, no index.

⚠️ **The contention was real but it was a different thing**: the #16929 round did hit a genuine collision in `step18.rationale`, where two retirements each append a paragraph. That is ordinary text, resolved by a merge, ⛔ not by serializing rounds. So the correct instruction is "merge and resolve", which is what this dispatch carries — and the four-way serialization I imposed was an unnecessary delay built on a mechanism I had not read.

⭐ Recording it in full because the cost was real: this card sat undispatched for ~90 minutes on a hazard that does not exist, and the only reason it surfaced is that a dev round read the file I had only reasoned about.

## Scope

Ruling-free and mechanical, and the card fences the ruling-grade question off itself:

> ⛔ No claim the conversions should delete the node. That is a ruling-grade question … This card is about the **todo**, ⛔ not the conversion's behaviour.

⇒ a step-18 **D3 semantic TODO** for the bare `element:filter` / `element:form` node the two D2 conversions leave behind, plus moving that PR's ADR-0087 disposition from `not-required (already-registered …)` to `registered` — the ids it names registered the **key strips**, ⛔ not the node deletion that became a required step.

## File face declared

`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/` (a new entry file), the generated `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts` region, and the ADR-0087 disposition. ⛔ Declared NOT touched: the two D2 conversions' behaviour, and `packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts` beyond what the generator rewrites.

⚠️ **Live overlap, declared**: PR #17835 (#16929) is open and appends to the same `step18.rationale` prose. It is parked — its card went to the decision box at 10:10Z over a release-shaping question — so this round ⛔ does not wait on it, and instead merges `origin/main` before opening its PR and expects that paragraph to conflict when #17835 eventually lands. ⛔ Do not edit #17835's paragraph; keep both intents when resolving.
